B: Hi! Right, are we on? Yeah, I can see you. I'm Nicola.
A: Hiya. Gemma.
B: Where are you, Gemma?
A: Ipswich.
B: Oh, right, Suffolk. I'm Woodley, near Reading. I'm meant to be working, to be honest, I've snuck this in between two Teams calls. Did you do that puzzle at the start?
A: Yeh. I did alright, I think. Couldn't tell you what it was for.
B: No, me neither. I just bashed through it. So what do you do?
A: I'm a senior care assistant. Residential home, forty beds. I run the shift, do the meds, that sort of thing.
B: Oh God, fair play. My dad's starting to need a bit of help, actually, and I'll be honest, I couldn't do it. Is it nights and all that?
A: Long days mostly. Four or five twelve-hour shifts a week. I do nights when we're short, which is a lot. I'm knackered most of the time, to be fair.
B: I bet. I do long hours but it's sitting on my backside, so I can't really moan. Well, I do moan.
A: What is it you do?
B: SAP consultant. Finance systems. So basically a big company wants to move all their accounts onto a new system and they get me in to make it actually work. I'm on a contract in Bracknell at the moment, it's a logistics firm, and it's chaos, honestly. Half the people in the workshops don't know what their own process is, so I'm sat there going, sorry, who signs this off? And nobody knows.
A: Right.
B: You'd think they'd pay a fortune for it, and they do, to be fair. That's why I contract. I wouldn't go permanent now, you'd have to drag me.
A: We've got agency staff come in like that. They get paid more than us for the same shift. Do you know what I mean? And half of them don't know the residents.
B: Yeah, that's the thing though, isn't it, the agency's always going to pay more, that's the market.
A: It's not a market, they're people's nans.
B: No, fair enough. Fair enough. I didn't mean it like that.
A: I know. It just gets me. Care's paid rubbish and everyone acts like anyone could do it.
B: I genuinely couldn't. I'd be useless. I can't even keep a plant alive, my cleaner does that. Have you got kids?
A: No. Just me and Lee, my partner, and the dog.
B: What sort of dog?
A: Staffy. Bella. She's old now, her back legs have gone a bit. That's her in the picture behind me.
B: Oh yeah, I can see. Bless her. I've got a fifteen-year-old, which is basically the same thing. Feed him and he grunts at you. He's got his mocks and he will not revise. I said to him, I'm not paying for a holiday in the summer if you fail the lot, and he just went, whatever.
A: Did he believe you?
B: No, course he didn't. I'd go anyway. We did Mauritius last year, it was unreal. Do you go away much?
A: Caravan in Norfolk most years. Hemsby. And Tenerife every couple of years, same hotel.
B: Same hotel? Don't you want to try somewhere different?
A: Not really. I know it's nice, I know the food's alright. I don't see the point going somewhere just to say you've been.
B: Ha, that's me told. No, I get it, I do. I just get bored.
A: Is that what you wanted, like, as a question? I'm not much good at small talk.
B: No, you're fine, honestly, you're more interesting than my two o'clock. So, yeah. What's the worst bit, then? Of the job?
